Or like the full moon. Having visualized this syllable, one again forms the Vajra-fist mudrā:
with the left hand, press the base of the ring finger with the thumb, and clench the remaining four fingers around the thumb to form a fist.

This seal can eliminate internal and external obstacles and defilements, and bring about the accomplishment of all merits. Holding a rosary in the right hand, one then recites the purification mantra aloud.
The Dharmadhātu Mantra. Recite twenty-one times. The mantra is:
Oṃ-lam (or it is also acceptable to hold only the syllable *laṃ*; *laṃ* may also be written as *raṃ*). [This is the Sanskrit syllable *oṃ-laṃ*.
This syllable *laṃ* of the pure Dharmadhātu—if one contemplates or recites it—can cause the three karmas to become entirely purified. All...
All karmic obstructions will be completely eliminated. Furthermore, one will be able to accomplish all superior matters. Wherever one dwells, that place shall become entirely pure.
If clothing is impure, it shall become pure clothing; if the body has not been bathed, it shall be as if bathed.
If one uses water alone to perform purification, it is not called true purity. If one purifies it by means of this *dharmadhātu-citta* and the syllable *LAṂ*, it is then called ultimate [purity].
The ultimate vessel of purity is like a single grain of elixir that transforms iron into gold; a single syllable of mantra transforms defilement into purity.
As the verse says: "The letter RA is brilliant white, adorned with the bindu of emptiness."
Place a nasal bindu above the letter *ra* in the Sanskrit script; it then becomes the syllable *laṃ*.
Like a bright jewel in a topknot placed upon the crown of the head, this mantra is identical to the Dharma-realm and eliminates immeasurable multitudes of sins.
In all cases of contact with impure places, one should apply this gateway of letters (*akṣaramukha*). Thus, the *Lotus Family Recitation Method* states:

"If one contacts an impure place, one should visualize the letter *DHĪḤ*, which is the source of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), upon the crown of one's head, emitting red light; that is to say, the letter *LAṂ*."
If external conditions are truly lacking—such as the absence of water for bathing or the lack of new, clean robes—one uses this syllable *laṃ* to purify oneself.

However, if external conditions are available yet one fails to bathe or change clothes, relying on this [syllable] alone to claim purity, such a person is one who lacks reverence, faith, and diligence;
they cannot even avoid the transgression of contempt, let alone extinguish sins, generate merit, or achieve accomplishment.

Regarding the *siddhi* sought: if one first bathes according to the ritual using water to cleanse oneself, puts on new, clean garments, and further purifies them with this mantra, then both internally and externally one will become completely pure; what is prayed for will then swiftly yield spiritual efficacy.
Next, recite the mantra for protecting the body. One should form the second root mudrā of the primary scripture and recite the heart-mantra seven times;
or else, one may form the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Aparājita and recite the Aparājita mantra seven times.
Nowadays, many recite mantras from other sections, namely the single-syllable mantra of Mañjuśrī.
Oṃ. *Ciliṃ* (The character *liṃ* should be pronounced with a retroflex *r* sound; it may also be transliterated as *jílíng*). (This is the Sanskrit syllable *oṃ ciliṃ*.
There are two original forms of this in Sanskrit script, much like the *lì* and *zhuàn* scripts here in China.

This *ciliṃ* may be read as a disyllabic (*erhé*) or trisyllabic (*sānhé*) combination, such as *cīrlíng*, or as a tetrasyllabic (*sìhé*) combination, such as *tǐlǐhìyín*. Master Yìjìng translated it as *chì*.
*Lo-he-ye-m*. These four syllables combined form a single word, which constitutes one character of the Sanskrit language.
For those who are not proficient in the Sanskrit language, it is truly difficult to attain its genuine subtlety. The power of this one-syllable King of Mantras is exceedingly great and inconceivable.
As stated in the *Mañjuśrī-mūla-ekākṣara-dhāraṇī-vidhi*: "The World-Honored One addressed the assembly of devas..."
He said: "One should know that among all dhāraṇīs, this is the great king of dhāraṇīs and possesses great supernormal power.
If any son or daughter of good family can receive and uphold it, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva will constantly come to protect them."
Whether during the waking state or within dreams, it manifests bodily forms and various auspicious matters;
this mantra is capable of summoning even Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, let alone other bodhisattvas and the assembly of mundane and supramundane worthies and sages.
This mantra can eliminate all five heinous crimes, the four grave offenses, and the karmic retribution of the ten evil deeds.
One should know that among all worldly and world-transcending mantras, this is the most supreme; it is the heart-essence of all Buddhas and can cause all one's aspirations to be fulfilled.
All shall be fully accomplished. Even before the ritual is performed, one can achieve all matters according to one's wishes.
If one generates the unsurpassed mind of great bodhicitta and recites it once, its power can protect oneself. If one recites it twice, its power can protect one’s companions.
If one recites it three times, its power can protect everyone within a single residence. If one recites it four times...
Its power is such that it can protect the people within a single city. If recited five times, its power can protect the people within a single kingdom.
If recited six times, its power can protect the people within a single world-system (*cāturdvīpaka*). If recited seven times, its power can protect the people within the four continents.
If one recites it once at dawn and uses enchanted water to wash one’s face, it can cause all who see one to rejoice.

Joy. It continues, saying: "If there are sentient beings seized by a 'flying-head' ghost (piṭaka-śīrṣa), they should rub their own faces with their hands and recite this mantra one hundred and eight times. [The ghost] will then assume a terrifying appearance.

Thereupon, the practitioner should form the *pūrvajanma-mudrā* with the left hand—bending the thumb into the palm and pressing the four fingers down upon the thumb, then clenching the fist tightly—and stare with wide-open eyes while secretly reciting this mantra; thus the affliction shall be expelled."

The ailment will be immediately removed. If one suffers from any illness caused by ghosts, one should recite the mantra over the right hand one hundred and eight times and burn *agallochum* incense while fumigating it.
With the left hand forming the *jātaka-mudrā*, one should rub the patient’s head with the right hand; the ailment will then be cured.
If one wishes to pass through places of peril, such as those inhabited by lions, tigers, wolves, venomous snakes, enemies, or bandits, [one should do so].
One must completely devote one's body and mind [to this practice]. One must not approach women, nor consume the five pungent roots, nor any alcohol or meat.
Toward all sentient beings, one should give rise to thoughts of great compassion and recite the mantra with a sincere heart forty-nine times. Then, as for those who are hostile and malicious—
They will naturally retreat and disperse. Even if they should encounter this mantra, there are none who do not rejoice.
If all sentient beings were to hear even the name of this mantra for a single kalpa, or for immeasurable kalpas, it would be impossible; how much more so to actually behold it?

Recite this dhāraṇī with single-minded devotion. It can cause sentient beings to always obtain peace and security in both the present life and future lives, and to be constantly accompanied by all Tathāgatas and the assembly of great Bodhisattvas as their retinue. Therefore, you should earnestly regard it as something difficult to encounter.
Do not give rise to contempt or doubt; as explained extensively in the sutras, these details are not recorded here at length.
An alternative translation states: "If one recites it one hundred times, one can protect a single kingdom; if one recites it one thousand times, one can protect the four continents.
Once one has recited this King of One-Syllable Mantras, one should further recite the Six-Syllable Great Illumination Mantra. One...
One hundred and eight times. Thereafter, one should recite the Cundī Dhāraṇī.

Fearing that it might now become overly mixed with other sections, causing practitioners to find it difficult to maintain, this has not been recorded here. If one wishes to maintain it, one should recite it as follows.

Next, recite the mantra for empowering the rosary. Apply powdered incense to the beads, hold the rosary with both palms at the heart, and recite the mantra seven times to empower it. The mantra is as follows:
Having empowered the *maṇi* with "Oṃ vairocana-maṇe svāhā," one makes this vow with mind and speech:

"I now wish to perform recitation; may the original deity, the Buddhas, and the Bodhisattvas empower and protect me, so that [my practice] may quickly accord with my wishes and all that I seek be fulfilled. Thereafter, with the left hand...
Hold the beads with the ring finger and the thumb of the left hand. With the thumb and ring finger of the right hand, move the beads while positioned before the heart.
With a tranquil mind, visualize the Buddha-Mother Cundī clearly and distinctly, seated facing you, surrounded by her retinue.
When reciting the Cundī mantra, the voice should be neither too slow nor too fast; at every utterance of the word *svāhā*, [the visualization should be maintained].
At the same time, move one bead [of the rosary]. Whether it be one hundred and eight recitations or one thousand and eighty recitations, there must always be a fixed limit;
it must not be deficient or omitted. If one is occupied with busy affairs, after completing one hundred and eight recitations, one may thereafter hold the beads loosely as desired.

Alternatively, one may bind the fundamental great seal (*mūla-mahāmudrā*) upon the arm of the Bodhisattva and count the recitations while chanting. Upon completion, [place it] upon the crown of the head.

The mudrā for scattering. When one hundred and eight [recitations] are completed, if one is unable to maintain further mindfulness, one may form the Vajra Fist mudrā with the left hand and hold the rosary with the right hand while reciting. The root mantra is as follows:
Namo satvānāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhakoṭīnām | tadyathā | oṃ cale cule cuṇḍe svāhā || (This is the Cundī mantra in Sanskrit script.)
If you wish for the matters you seek to be swiftly accomplished, you should rely on the ritual procedures of the original sūtra as described above;

only by abstaining from alcohol, meat, and pungent vegetables will you obtain the desired response. If you wish to obtain benefits at any time, such as the extinguishing of sins and the generation of merit, those living at home who cannot completely renounce alcohol, meat, and spouses may recite it on the ten days of fasting (the *shizhai*). If you wish to maintain this practice continuously...

Regarding those who practice with interruptions— meaning on days other than the ten days of the *zhāirì* (fasting days)— even if they possess wine, meat, wives, or concubines, as long as they single-mindedly recite and uphold [the mantra],
it can cause those with short lifespans to increase their years and cause illnesses to be eliminated.
In the sūtras and vinayas, it is stated that those living as householders are unable to maintain the precepts and fasts for long periods;

therefore, they are instructed to observe the eightfold *śīla* fast (*upoṣadha*) on ten days each month, abstaining from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, intoxicants, perfumes and flowers, singing, dancing, and amusements.

The eight precepts constitute the *śīla*, while abstaining from food after midday constitutes the *upavāsa*. By thus purely observing the *upavāsa* and *śīla* for ten days, one should recite the mantra;

thereby, one will certainly obtain swift efficacy. In the present age, people do not understand the *upavāsa* and *śīla*, but instead mistakenly regard merely abstaining from alcohol and meat as the *upavāsa*.
This has been an error for a long time. As for the allowance of consuming alcohol, meat, and keeping a wife and concubines while performing recitations, this is due to [the influence of] recent...

The customs of the age flow toward wine, meat, wives, and concubines; these constitute their habitual occupation. Although they may hear the Buddha’s precepts, their ingrained natures are difficult to change.
If one does not employ this great, inconceivable divine mantra to rescue and deliver them, on what day shall they attain liberation from birth and death?
Therefore, the *Buddhōṣṇīṣa-stotra* says: "Those who do not observe the fast are called observers of the fast; those who do not uphold the precepts are called upholders of the precepts. If...
Upon hearing the *Uṣṇīṣa-buddhamanusmṛti-dhāraṇī*, one immediately attains the precepts of the voice.
For those who maintain the purity of the fast and precepts and recite it according to the Dharma, how could they not swiftly transcend birth and death?
There may be those who lack merit and auspicious marks, who fail in their pursuit of office and are oppressed by poverty and suffering;

if they constantly recite this mantra, it can cause them to obtain in this very life the blessings of a Wheel-Turning King (Cakravartin). Whatever official rank they seek will surely be attained as desired.

If they seek wisdom, sons, daughters, or other things, there is nothing that will not accord with their wishes. This mantra is like a *maṇi* jewel: everything is obtained according to one's heart's desire.

One shall obtain all things. Even if one wishes to invite Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, or the Son of Heaven Yama, by merely reciting this mantra, they will surely arrive according to the invitation.
Whatever tasks are assigned, they will be carried out in accordance with one's own heart's wish. This mantra possesses great power within Jambudvīpa;
it can move Mount Sumeru, dry up the waters of the great ocean, and cause flowers to bloom upon withered wood through its incantation.

If this is so, how much more so for one who can further recite according to the ritual; without changing their physical body, they will attain great supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*), go to Tuṣita Heaven to hear the True Dharma, travel to the worlds of the ten directions to serve the Buddhas, and receive the prediction of enlightenment (*bodhy-avyākaraṇa*).
If one wishes to accomplish the mandala rite, perform it according to the sūtra as previously described; or, using only a mirror-mandala, one may take a new [mirror].
Regarding a mirror that has never been used: before an image of the Buddha, starting from the night of the fifteenth day of the month, face the east and place the mirror before its stand.
Adorn it with offerings according to one's means, providing various incenses, flowers, and pure *argha* water.
Then, forming the fundamental great mudrā at the level of the heart, recite the fundamental mantra over the mirror one hundred and eight times.
Place the mirror inside a pouch and always carry it with you. Whenever you wish to perform recitation, simply set the mirror-altar before you, form the mudrā, and recite the mantra.
If you cannot recite facing the mirror every day, you may do so facing the mirror on the ten days of the *zhāi* (fasting) observances;
on other days, it is also permissible to recite without facing the mirror. If you have no mirror, simply visualize a mirror situated before you.
Recitation also brings accomplishment. For those who are unable to perform the visualization, simply focusing one's mind on the recitation alone will also lead to success.
This Cundī Dhāraṇī was spoken by seventy-seven koṭis of Tathāgatas. The Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna praised it with these verses:
Those who constantly recite this *Cundī-dhāraṇī*, a treasury of merit, with a tranquil mind, cannot be harmed by any great calamities.
Whether in the heavens or among humans, they shall receive blessings equal to those of a Buddha.
Having encountered this wish-fulfilling jewel, they will certainly attain the state that is peerless.
Nowadays, following the Cundī mantra, many also recite the mantra of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Ekākṣara Mahācakra Vidyārāja, namely the syllable *buṃ*.
This is the Sanskrit syllable *buṃ*;
it is also pronounced with the retroflex tongue-tip (*ūṣman*), and these two syllables are combined as one.
It is written as one character. It is also written as *bùlín* (步林), or as [口*普][口*(隆-一)] (普隆). It is also written as *bùlǒng* (部隴) and *bólóng* (勃龍).

The Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra translated it as *bōlú'ān* (勃嚕唵), combining three characters into one. His commentary states: "The character *lú* (嚕) is pronounced with the tongue rolled back, forming a single sound.
Furthermore, he cites that the sound issues from the chest and throat; its resonance is like that of a large bell being struck."
"Drum. The ancient translation was "Bulin," which is an erroneous and incorrect rendering. If this were the case, it would be difficult to obtain the correct pronunciation;
only those well-versed in the Sanskrit sounds can achieve this.

The *Mūlavidhi-sūtra* states: "This One-Syllable Vidyārāja of the Great Wheel of the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa, for one who attains its accomplishment, can perform the deeds of a Buddha even when the Dharma of all Tathāgatas is about to perish.
Furthermore, it can protect the entire treasury of the Dharma of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas. This One-Syllable Vidyārāja shall circulate during the final age after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa."
In this world, there are no mantras superior to these, which have been received and upheld by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
and were transmitted by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past. Furthermore, wherever a practitioner may be who single-mindedly recites this Great Vidya,
within a radius of five yojanas in that location, among all things within the realm of earth...
All malevolent planetary deities (*nakṣatra*) will be unable to approach; all evil spirits and ghosts (*bhūta* and *yakṣa*) will scatter in every direction;
and even all manner of evils will be unable to cause harm. As for devas and sages, they too will not dare to draw near.
If one maintains and recites this, all karmic obstructions (*karmāvaraṇa*) shall become purified. If used for protection, it can enable one to remain hidden and enter among all classes of beings.
Among many, it is unobstructed; it cannot be harmed by anything mundane or supramundane.
This mantra can destroy all evil spells of the world. It is the crown of all Buddhas and the heart of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
It can bestow fearlessness upon all sentient beings and grant happiness to all sentient beings. For anyone who practices...
If one maintains this, one shall obtain fruits according to one's wishes, just like a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*), capable of fulfilling all aspirations.
If any other mantra one recites fails to achieve success, one should employ this *dhāraṇī* together with that mantra in one place and recite and maintain them simultaneously;
it will certainly achieve success. If there is no success or spiritual efficacy, the deity of that mantra shall have its head split into seven pieces.
It should be known that this mantra can assist all other mantras so that they quickly attain accomplishment.

If one wishes to seek the accomplishment of all dharmas by reciting this mantra alone, one should perform the ritual and recitation according to that sūtra. As for the practitioner who maintains and recites it:
If one is unable to recite the Mantra of the Pure Dharma Realm, the Mantra for Protecting the Body, and so forth,
up to the One-Syllable Mahācakra Mantra as previously described, one may instead single-mindedly uphold this Cundī Dhāraṇī. If, due to old age or physical decline,
one’s strength is insufficient to recite the complete mantra, one may first recite it three times and thereafter begin only from the syllable *Oṃ*.
One may also recite the following nine characters. Furthermore, if one is unable to form the Great Seal of Cundī, one should instead perform the recitation with the Vajra Fist.
Upon completing the recitation of the mantra, one should again employ the Vajra Fist Seal and recite the HŪṂ mantra while sealing the five places:
first seal the forehead, next seal the right shoulder, next seal the left shoulder, next seal the heart, and finally seal [the back of the head].
Above the throat. Having completed the mudrās, scatter them upon the crown of the head. This can eliminate all demonic obstacles and accomplish all supreme matters.
Furthermore, wherever one dwells, if one wishes to expel spirits and deities, one may form the Vajradhātu mudrā;
simply recite the Cundī Dhāraṇī twenty-one times over scented water and sprinkle it in the eight directions, above, and below. By so sprinkling, the boundary for expulsion is established.

The *Vidyādharapiṭaka-vidhi* states: "If, while performing the ritual, one falls asleep within the maṇḍala or experiences a bad dream, one should immediately recite the Buddhalocanā mantra eight hundred times.
While reciting, hold the rosary in the right hand and grasp the vajra with the left hand. The mantra is: Oṃ dhuna vajra haḥ."
When reciting daily according to the ritual, one must fix the specific times. If recited once, it should be at dawn;
if twice, then including evening; if thrice, then adding midday. For those with busy affairs who cannot follow these fixed times, they may recite whenever they have leisure.
If practiced by those of superior faculties, they shall attain the three [bodies].
The Secret Correspondences: First, the secret of body (sitting upright and forming mudrās); second, the secret of speech (reciting mantras aloud); third, the secret of mind.

This involves single-minded concentration, which may consist of visualizing the Sanskrit letters of the mantra, focusing on the sound of the recitation, visualizing the sacred countenance of Cundī, or visualizing the vajra, flask, flowers, fruits, and other objects held in the hands of the Bodhisattva.
The *Commentary on the Sūtra of Divine Transformations* states: "If one takes the three secrets as the gateway, there is no need to pass through kalpas or fully cultivate all practices;
rather, one can fulfill all the pāramitās within this very life. Thus, the *Five Secret Ritual Manuals* says:
"With the three secrets of the Vajra as the predominant condition, one is able to realize the fruit of the pure three bodies of Vairocana. This is the explanation.

The *dhāraṇī* text states: "If there were any Buddhas who attained Buddhahood without cultivating the three mysteries (*triguhyamukha*) and without relying upon the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, such a thing is impossible.
If, after attaining Buddhahood, they were to have any cessation regarding the three mysteries and the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, such a thing is impossible.
Furthermore, when correctly reciting [the mantra], if one has not completed one hundred and eight repetitions..."
One must not engage in conversation with others. If one must indeed speak, one should visualize the letter *laṃ* of the Brahmī script upon one's own tongue;
even while speaking, the mantra will not be interrupted. Once the conversation is finished, one should immediately resume holding the previous [mantra]. Question:
Is it sufficient for the accomplishment of merit to hold only a single path of mantra, or should one instead extensively hold many paths of mantras?
He said, "The accomplishment of merit. He replied, "There are two gates to this. The first is the gate of according with the inclinations of the faculties.
This means that human faculties and capacities are of many kinds and their preferences differ; some may prefer to uphold the three paths, the five paths, or the ten paths."
Up to a hundred mantras and so forth; among these, one may recite whichever one accords with one's faculties and inclinations. Second is the gate of swiftly attaining accomplishment:
if one seeks all merits and desires to achieve them quickly, it is appropriate to single-mindedly recite the mantra of a single path.
When that is accomplished, the merits of all mantras will be fully realized. Thus, the Mañjuśrī-vidhi-sūtra says:
If one wishes to accomplish all meritorious virtues, one must not give rise to thoughts regarding other mantras as being [the primary means].
Although there are several paths of mantras mentioned above, they are all sequential stages for the recitation of the Cundī mantra.

This is for the purpose of accomplishing the supreme and wondrous. Furthermore, every day when facing a mirror and wishing to begin the recitation, one should, as prescribed in the original sutra, visualize one's own mind as a single lunar disc, perfectly bright and pure, with the nine sacred syllables in Sanskrit script.

One should imagine that each individual syllable emits various kinds of light, spreading throughout the brilliant clarity of the lunar disc of the mind. If one is unable to visualize these nine [syllables], [one should instead visualize...]

Regarding the syllables: one should visualize a single *oṃ* from the Brahmī script within the lunar disc of the heart, or alternatively, visualize nine Brahmī syllables arranged upon the various parts of one’s own body.
As for the statement that these nine Brahmī syllables possess manifold radiances, it is as stated in the verse from the version translated by Vajrajñāna:
"Visualize *oṃ* placed upon the head; its color is white like the moon, emitting immeasurable light, which dispels..."
Extinguishing all obstacles, one becomes equal to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. He strokes the crown of this person’s head;
the syllable *ja* is placed upon the two eyes, its color like the sun and moon, to illuminate all ignorant darkness and enable the arising of profound wisdom-light.

The syllable *li* is placed upon the neck, its color like deep blue lapis lazuli, able to manifest all forms and characteristics, gradually perfecting the wisdom of the Tathāgata. One should visualize the syllable *jhu* at the heart. Its...
The color is like pure white; because the mind is thus purified, one swiftly reaches the path to Bodhi. The syllable *LṚ* is placed upon the two shoulders; its color is yellow like gold.
By contemplating this form, one is able to don the armor of diligence. The syllable *ŚŪ* is visualized at the navel; its color is a wondrous pale yellow-white.
Because one does not regress from Bodhi, one swiftly ascends to the sublime site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). The syllable *TṚ* is placed upon the two thighs. Its...
The color is pale yellow; one will swiftly realize the path to Bodhi and attain the seat of Vajra. Place the syllable *Svā* on both shins;
its form is red, and by constantly visualizing this syllable, one will swiftly turn the wheel of Dharma. Place the syllable *Ha* on both feet.
Its color is like that of the full moon. When the practitioner forms this mental image, they will swiftly attain parinirvāṇa.

According to the *Xianmi yuantong* (The Perfect Penetration of Exoteric and Esoteric), one should arrange and visualize the syllables of the dhāraṇīs from various sections; however, I fear that for beginners, this may conversely prove even more difficult.
Therefore, one should rely on the fundamental school for the essential method of recitation.
Alternatively, if one wishes to visualize the meaning of other syllables, it should be done as clarified in a separate section at the end of this sūtra.

Furthermore, if one is unable to visualize these Sanskrit characters, simply reciting with single-minded devotion is likewise endowed with all samādhis. Thus, the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* states: "Dhāraṇī..."

This is the treasury of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), wherein hundreds of thousands of samādhis are constantly manifest before one. If, while one is earnestly reciting it, one encounters various demonic obstacles;
or if one suddenly feels fear; or if the mouth finds it difficult to recite; or if body and mind are uneasy; or if there is excessive anger or drowsiness;
or if one perceives various strange signs; or if doubt arises regarding the mantra such that one is unwilling to continue the recitation—[these are the impediments].
One should apply the remedial methods. One should form the second root mudrā according to this sūtra and recite the heart mantra;
or perform the mudrā of the Aparājita mantra; or contemplate the letter *ra* of the Brahmic script; or contemplate the letter *a*.
By performing any one of these methods or contemplating any one of these letters, those objective realms will naturally vanish. If one discriminates...

For those with a preponderance of mental activity, one should contemplate the syllable *sa*, which immediately brings about non-conceptuality. If one has a preponderance of attachment to conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta*), one should contemplate the syllable *haṃ*;
thus, one realizes that the fundamental nature of dependent origination is emptiness. Furthermore, the *Vidyādharapiṭaka-sūtra* states:

"When a practitioner wishes to perform a rite, they must first clarify the mind and distance themselves from all worldly clamor. Within their own person, they should visualize the subtle and wondrous..."
The characteristics of the syllables appear one by one before him. Once they have appeared before him, all sinful defilements are completely extinguished. Regarding the subtle and wondrous syllables:
first, one should visualize the syllable *Muṃ* at the opening of the mouth; visualize the syllable *Aṃ* on the right shoulder; visualize the syllable *Aḥ* on the left shoulder;
again, visualize the syllable *Aṃ* upon the head; and visualize [the syllable] on the right arm.
The syllable Ā. On the upper left arm, one should visualize the syllable Va.
In the navel wheel (*nābhi-cakra*), one should visualize the syllable Hūṃ. Furthermore, one should visualize the syllable Ā throughout the entire body.
Whenever the practitioner visualizes these syllables and they manifest upon the parts of the body, he should immediately recite the mantra: HŪṂ VAJRE KRODHE HŪṂ. This.
Mantra: If one recites this up to one *lakṣa*, all sins will be eliminated. Furthermore, the mantra is:
